items.label: Absci Morgan Stanley healthcare conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
items.signal_prefix: Platform and cost model (management): the roughly $15 million per program

set.signal: Platform and cost model (management): CFO: the $15 million per program includes all the work to generate a drug candidate and take it through R&D-enabling studies to make it Phase I ready. CEO: the Atlas agentic co-scientist is surfacing 5-plus new targets for different indications, and China lets Absci run trials at a tenth of the cost; CFO: the strategy is to leverage execution in China for proof-of-concept work and Phase II development going forward. CFO: the goal is to start an endometriosis Phase II study this year, and current cash runs through the ABS-201 headline readout (26-week data and one-year follow-up) and at least the endometriosis interim readout.

items.reason: Source says 'R&D enabling studies' (not IND-enabling) and 'generate a DC' (the $15M includes generating the candidate); China PoC/Phase II use is the CFO's forward strategy, not current CEO-stated execution.
items.evidence: The $15 million includes all the work to generate a DC, so a drug candidate, and then to take that through R&D enabling studies, so to make it phase I ready.

items.label: Absci Morgan Stanley healthcare conference 2026 (09-16-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CEO Sean McClain: Lilly's $40 million investment carries no rights
items.reason: Restates the Absci Q2 FY2026 (08-11-2026) contract on this edge ($40M investment, no rights to ABS-201, advisory-board seat); the only new content (no option/ROFN/governance rights) is equity-investment deal terms, which skill section 2 excludes as financing.
items.evidence: This was a $40 million investment, what I will call tickets to the game. They have no rights to the asset on both pattern hair loss as well as endometriosis.
